figures.title: Figure 1
figures.llm_description: Figure 1 Experimental setup and surface rippling. (a) A schematic demonstration  of the sample stacking and strain generated due to the heating/cooling of indium  which has been used as glue between WTe2 and Si substrate. (b) STM images of  several surface rippling at different sample locations. Scale bars are 50 nm.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.llm_description: Figure 2 Atomistic structure and STM images. (a) Side view of 3D Td-WTe2.  (b) Top view of 2D 1T’-WTe2. For clarity, different colors are used for the atoms  in (b): W, brown; higher Te on top surface (TeTH), blue; lower Te on top surface  (TeTL), orange; Te on bottom surface (TeB), grey. (c) High-resolution STM images  of pristine WTe2 surface at Vbias = 5 mV. (d) WTe2 surface with TDBs at Vbias =  2.08 V. (e) Atomically resolved image of TDBs at Vbias = 9.57 mV. (f) Atomic  structure of 1T’-WT

figures.title: Figure 4
figures.llm_description: Figure 4 Generalized stacking fault energy (GSFE) analysis. (Upper part) The  twin is obtained by rigidly sliding the upper half of a pristine 1T’-WTe2 along  the x direction sequentially, as indicated in frames I to VI. The twin region is  shaded blue. The unit length of 1T’-WTe2 in the [110] direction is defined as a0.
